body: A developer and its company, NSI6 LLC, asked a Benton County, Missouri judge for a temporary restraining order after county commissioners adopted a six-month moratorium on data centers on Aug. 10, 2026, KY3 reported. The moratorium allowed projects already under construction to continue. At a Sept. 2 hearing attended by about 100 people, the county argued the moratorium applied because the developer did not yet own the land, had not started the project and could still withdraw. The developer's attorney said the developer chose Benton County because it has no planning and zoning and understood there would be no restrictions when he began trying to buy the land; he had committed to the purchase on July 23, with closing set for Sept. 9, and testified that withdrawing would cost $100,000.

The judge granted the restraining order on Sept. 8, and the purchase of the roughly 12-acre property on old Highway 65 closed Sept. 9, KY3 reported. At a Sept. 21 hearing on whether to grant a preliminary injunction, the county's presiding commissioner testified that commissioners had met the developer in June about a possible data center at a different site and had no further contact, and the county argued the moratorium should stand because NSI6 LLC did not become a legal entity until Aug. 13, three days after the moratorium. The judge extended the restraining order and urged caution on construction until a final decision. The developer plans two buildings of about 20,000 square feet each.

The same company is also suing the City of Springfield over that city's data center moratorium, KY3 reported. In a Nov. 9 story on the Springfield case, KY3 reported that Benton County commissioners cannot enforce their moratorium until a final judgment is entered, and that no court date had been set in the Benton County case.

timeline.label: Developer commits to purchase land in Benton County for a data center project
Benton County commissioners adopt a six-month moratorium on data centers
Court hears the developer's request for a temporary restraining order
Judge grants a temporary restraining order against the moratorium
Developer closes on the roughly 12-acre property
Judge hears preliminary-injunction request and extends the TRO pending a final decision
